correctness.rationale: Headline claim: all 9331 ordered 3x3 margin classes (entries 0..6) and all 7140 ordered 3x4 classes (entries 0..4) have connected Diaconis-Sturmfels 2x2 fiber graphs with exact diameters as tabulated; 3x3 max is uniform (6,6,6)x(6,6,6) size 406 diam 12 (unique); 3x4 max diam 8 attained on 22 classes, exhibited witness r=(4,4,4) c=(0,4,4,4) size 120 with 9-table shortest path; largest 3x4 fiber uniform (4,4,4)x(3,3,3,3) size 415 diam 6. Verified: (1) class counts combinatorially (sum over equal row/col sums = 9331/7140) and CSV row counts 9331/7140; histogram sums match totals; diam-0 iff size-1 holds on all rows. (2) Ran committed verify.py: VERIFY_OK sizes=(406,120) diams=(12,8), including per-step rectangular 2x2-move check, margin check, BFS shortestness plus full-fiber coverage (connectivity), size agreement by independent row-composition enumerator, and spot diameters (406->12, 21->4, 415->6). (3) Independent recomputation with a separately written comps-product enumerator + independently built move set and BFS: 30 random classes with size<=60 (15+15) all match (size, connectivity, diameter); all 47 3x3 classes with diam>=10 recomputed exactly (confirms 12 unique at 666x666, nine 11s, 37 10s); all four size-120 diam-8 3x4 classes plus one rep of each (255,312) diam-8 group plus the 415-size class recomputed exactly. (4) Maximal paths manually QR-checked as valid single-rectangle moves with correct margins. This is proof by finite exhaustive enumeration with two independent enumerators and all-pairs BFS certificates, not heuristic evidence; classical DS connectivity theorem is honestly cited as prior art, not invoked as proof. No boundary error: zero-sum/singleton classes correctly give diam 0; directed moves counted as 18/36 consistent with undirected 9/18 rectangles.

originality.rationale: Nearest priors substantively compared: (a) Diaconis-Sturmfels (1998) proves 2x2 moves generate the toric ideal and hence connect every 2-way fiber -- theorem only, tabulates no diameters and no maximal-fiber path. Candidate builds on it and explicitly disclaims novelty of connectivity itself. (b) Aoki (2016) survey (abstract fetched live) reviews MCMC + Markov bases with Macaulay2/R fundamental examples -- no uniform diameter table or maximal witness for bounded 3x3/3x4 classes. (c) Hara-Aoki-Takemura (2011) states explicit bases known only for simple models and motivates small-model work -- provides no diameter table. (d) Markov Bases Database (298 entries, fetched live): schema records N/dim/state-space/Markov degree/minimal size/symmetry classes plus .mar files -- bare bases and counts, no fiber-graph diameter column and no maximal-fiber path witness. Diameters are not mechanically implied by the classical degree-2 basis theorem; each requires per-fiber BFS enumeration. No live source records the claimed uniform exact diameter tables, distributions, or witnesses. Fiber sizes of isolated margins may be individually computable, but the uniform diameter census plus shortest-path witnesses are new as a table.

value.rationale: Headline is a rigorously established exact invariant (fiber-graph diameter, plus size and witness paths) of natural objects (fixed-margin 3x3/3x4 contingency fibers under the standard DS move set). Object and invariant were motivated before computation: fiber diameters govern MCMC mixing for exact conditional tests in the Diaconis-Sturmfels program, usable to calibrate mixing expectations and validate samplers on small margins. Values were not known or mechanically implied (require per-fiber enumeration; e.g. max 12 vs largest-fiber diam 6 is non-obvious). A future researcher can reasonably need the precise facts (maximal diameters 12 and 8, full distributions, endpoint witnesses, per-class CSV). Scope (margins<=6/<=4) is the smallest nontrivial 2-way window where full BFS is feasible -- model-size-determined, not result-tuned -- and the census is complete within its stated bounds (0 disconnected, all classes tabulated), so no incomplete-census discount applies. Not a textbook restatement (connectivity theorem itself is prior art and disclaimed), not a parameter substitution, not an unexplained enumeration (diameters + paths + mixing interpretation supplied).

decisive_checks: Ran committed verify.py in inputs/artifacts: VERIFY_OK sizes=(406,120) diams=(12,8); witness rectangularity, margins, BFS shortestness + full coverage, spot diameters all pass.
Combinatorial class-count check: ordered margin pairs with equal sums = 9331 (3x3,b=6) and 7140 (3x4,b=4); CSV row counts and both histogram totals agree; diam-0 iff size-1 on every row.
Independent recomputation (separately written comps enumerator + rebuilt moves + BFS): 30 random size<=60 classes (15 per shape) all match CSV (size, connectivity, diameter).
Full independent recompute of all 47 3x3 classes with diam>=10: all match, confirming unique diam-12 class 666x666 and 11/10 counts 9/37.

Independent recompute of all four size-120 diam-8 3x4 classes + one rep each of (255,312) diam-8 groups + uniform 415-size class (diam 6): all match; CSV scan confirms 22 classes at diam 8 and largest fiber 415 at diam 6.
Fetched Aoki abstract and Markov Bases DB schema live to confirm absence of any diameter table or witness field. CSV scan confirms max-size/max-diam rows and DRAFT distribution strings.
residual_risks: Common-mode bug: census.py and verify.py are both stdlib Python written for the same rectangular-move geometry; independent enumerators agree and per-step geometry is asserted, but a shared misreading of adjacency (excluded pathological moves) would affect both. Mitigated by definitional move check per path step and analytic agreement with the classical 2-way connectivity theorem.

Originality rests on live search (admission review + auditor fetch of survey abstract and DB schema); an obscure thesis/table with identical diameters cannot be logically excluded, but no such table was found and diameters require per-fiber BFS not present in basis galleries.
No claim beyond the bounded margins: no general diameter formula or larger-margin guarantee is offered or should be inferred.
